title: What Happens When One Tiny Brain Patch Builds Whole Faces?
description:
Clinical Case Briefing — Nancy Kanwisher (1997): The Fusiform Face Area (FFA), Upside-Down 'Thatcher' Blindness & Domain Specificity, grounded in Nancy Kanwisher, Josh McDermott, Marvin M. Chun (1997) (The Journal of Neuroscience). Empirical findings show that in 1997 at the MGH NMR Center, Nancy Kanwisher, Josh McDermott, and Marvin Chun scanned 15 individual subjects in fMRI rather than blurring brains together by group-averaging — discovering a ~1-cubic-centimeter region on the lateral ventral fusiform gyrus (strongest in the right hemisphere) present in 12 of 15 individuals.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how primary visual cortex, fusiform face area, temporal lobe coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that to prove this 'Fusiform Face Area' (FFA) wasn't just reacting to low-level contrast, curves, animate body parts, or general attention, Kanwisher threw FIVE ruthless control tests at it in a single paper.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Nancy Kanwisher, Josh McDermott, Marvin M. Chun (1997). The Fusiform Face Area: A Module in Human Extrastriate Cortex Specialized for Face Perception. The Journal of Neuroscience. https://doi.org/10.1523/jneurosci.17-11-04302.1997
- Nancy Kanwisher, Frank Tong, Ken Nakayama (1998). The effect of face inversion on the human fusiform face area. Cognition. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0010-0277(98)00035-3
- Nancy Kanwisher, Damian Stanley, Alison Harris (1999). The fusiform face area is selective for faces not animals. NeuroReport. https://doi.org/10.1097/00001756-199901180-00035

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
